title: How a water heater works
caption: The tank in your basement is fighting fire, rust and pressure all day 🔥🚿 #howitsbuilt #waterheater #plumbing #homeowner #howitworks

lines.text: Every hot shower you take starts in a tank that's been keeping water hot all day.
So you start with a big steel tank, often fifty gallons.
But bare steel rusts when it sits in water.
So the inside gets coated with a thin layer of *glass*.
Then a gas *burner* underneath heats the water, and the hot exhaust rises through a pipe up the middle, warming it even more.
But cold water coming in would mix right into the hot water at the top.
So a *dip tube* carries it straight down to the bottom, and the hot water rises to the outlet on top.
A *thermostat* turns the burner off once the water is hot enough.
But the glass gets tiny cracks, and rust starts eating the steel.
So you hang an *anode rod* inside, a metal stick that rusts away instead of the tank.
But if the thermostat ever fails, the water keeps heating, and the pressure keeps climbing.
So a *relief valve* pops open and lets it out before the tank can burst.
And minerals settle on the bottom as *sediment*, so you drain some out once a year.
Then you wrap it all in foam, so the heat stays in.
Congratulations, you just built a *water heater*.
